BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Scope note:** I have only the Seller's cover note, Seller Update summary and Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the full SPA, so the Seller's clause numbers may not match the draft's, and some points need checking against the mark-up. Nothing below is a confirmed position. Where the Seller says something is "negotiated", "settled", "agreed" or "fair", I treat that as the Seller's assertion, not a cleared position (Playbook 0.4 / 6.3).

## 1. Summary of Material Departures

| # | Issue | Playbook position | Seller position | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap (12.1) | 25% / AUD 6.0m starting; 20% / AUD 4.8m only with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **Reject as presented.** The number matches our fallback, but no authority has been given, so it is not cleared. |
| 2 | De minimis / basket (12.2) | AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k basket, first-dollar recovery once exceeded | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket; excess-only recovery | **Reject.** Five times our de minimis, five times our basket, and a deductible rather than a tipping basket. |
| 3 | General claims period (12.3/13) | 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost approval | 18 months | **Reject.** Requires approval we have not given. |
| 4 | Limitation applies to all claims (12.3/13) | Separate regimes; Title/Fundamental outside general limits | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded | **Reject.** This is a hidden general-regime override. |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title (Seller's "administrative simplicity") | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | **Reject.** Core playbook point. |
| 6 | Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of these | Apply to all Claims of any nature; no fraud carve-out | **Reject.** Fraud carve-out is non-negotiable and cannot be waived. |
| 7 | Disclosure (Schedule 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure | Disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records | **Reject.** Materially broadens what the Buyer is deemed to know. |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Delete blanket knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Buyer has no claim for anything known or discoverable from the data room or public records | **Reject.** Effectively a data-room disclosure by another route. |
| 9 | Bluefen consent (3/6.3; DL 2) | Effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer consent | Reasonable endeavours; treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's consent. DL confirms no final consent or condition evidence yet. | **Reject.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). Consent-on-delivery is not acceptable. |
| 10 | Riverlark (2/7; DL 3) | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases. Post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Release to be provided after Completion | **Reject.** Post-completion release needs the undertaking and Amelia Frost approval. The ~AUD 3.2m facility should be repaid from Completion funds. |
| 11 | Employee bonuses (DL 5; funds flow) | DD-005 AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs must be a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded | Excluded from funds flow; "a matter for the Seller"; on-costs not addressed | **Reject.** Funds flow must not silently exclude them. |
| 12 | Ironquay IP (11.1; DL 4) | Broaden the narrow indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180k not independently verified either way | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | **Reject.** Narrow scope. Broaden it while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism. |
| 13 | Export/privacy incident (4.6/Sch 6; DL 6) | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way. | "Not expected to be material" | **Push back on characterisation.** Use neutral language. Do not accept "not material" as a finding. Require preserved logs and investigation updates. |
| 14 | Sandbar renewals (DL 8; AUD 330k) | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | **Assess, don't accept.** The DL itself says it does not establish whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| 15 | Tax / IP warranties | Remain open; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed | "Settled under the general regime" | **Reject.** Both are open. No general-regime override. |
| 16 | Title (DL 10; DD-012) | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source only | Title evidenced by Company share register at DD-012 | **Reject as sufficient.** The register is an internal Seller document, not independent proof. |
| 17 | Office lease (DL 7), Mossvale (DL 9) | Not addressed specifically in playbook excerpt | Notice/assignment restrictions noted; consent not stated to be required | **Confirm.** Ask for a legal review of whether landlord or Mossvale consent is needed for the share sale. Do not accept DL 1.4 non-admission as a substitute for analysis. |

## 2. Reasoning on Key Issues

**Caps, thresholds and time limits (items 1 to 3).** The Seller's package is close to our fallback on the cap but worse than our starting position on everything else. The 20%/AUD 4.8m cap is the conditional fallback, which can only be offered with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. Matching a fallback number does not clear it. The thresholds are much higher and use a deductible, so the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of claims. The 18-month period is also a fallback requiring approval.

**Structural risk (items 4 to 8).** The most serious issues are structural rather than numeric. A single "any limitation applies to all Claims" rule, a non-reliance and exclusive-remedy clause with no fraud carve-out, a broad disclosure of the data room and public records, and a buyer knowledge bar together would strip the Buyer of recourse for matters we did not agree to bear. Fundamental/Title claims are the one area where the playbook is firm: 100% cap, six years, and no knowledge bar. The Seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale does not justify folding them into general limits.

**Completion conditions and funds (items 9 to 11).** Bluefen is the largest commercial risk. A revenue-critical consent should be effective and evidenced before Completion, not treated as satisfied on delivery. Riverlark should be repaid from Completion funds. The funds flow should show the AUD 420k bonuses and related on-costs, or the Seller should fund them. Silent exclusion would shift a known liability to the Buyer.

**Specific matters (items 12 to 14).** The Ironquay indemnity is narrower than the matter warrants. The AUD 180k figure is not independently verified either way, so we should not treat it as either a confirmed debt or a cleared amount. The export incident should be neither confirmed nor dismissed. The Seller's "not expected to be material" wording is an opinion, not a finding. The Sandbar renewals should be assessed on their terms, not classified as ordinary course or deducted from price.

**Open points and evidence (items 15 to 17).** Tax and IP are open and cannot be treated as resolved under the general regime. Title needs independent evidence. The lease and Mossvale points need legal analysis before we accept the Seller's framing.

## 3. Recommendations

**Push back on (reject):**
1. Any cap above AUD 4.8m, and do not accept 20%/AUD 4.8m as cleared without written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft.
2. The AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k basket and excess-only recovery. Revert to AUD 5k, AUD 50k and first-dollar recovery.
3. The 18-month general claims period. Hold at 24 months unless Amelia Frost approves otherwise in writing.
4. The "any limitation applies to all Claims" rule. Keep the regimes separate.
5. Folding Fundamental/Title into general caps and time limits. Restore 100% cap, six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
6. The application of limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. Carve these out to the maximum extent enforceable.
7. Whole-data-room, public-register and statutory-register deemed disclosure (Schedule 7; DL 1.1, 1.2). Require specific fair disclosure.
8. Clause 8.3 buyer knowledge. Delete it, or restrict any qualifier to named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
9. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours for Bluefen. Require effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion.
10. Riverlark release after Completion. Require repayment from Completion funds. If a post-completion release is ever considered, it needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
11. Exclusion of the AUD 420k bonuses and on-costs from the funds flow. Require a specific line item or Seller funding.
12. The narrow Ironquay indemnity. Broaden it while preserving the SOW3 cure.
13. The "ordinary course" and "settled" characterisations for Sandbar, tax and IP. Treat them as open.
14. Reliance on DD-012 as proof of title. Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence.

**Request from the Seller:**
- Final Bluefen consent and evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Riverlark payout figure, discharge documents and security release mechanics.
- Confirmation of the Ironquay SOW3 payment position, with receipts or confirmatory assignment.
- Export incident: preserved logs, investigation scope, and regular written updates.
- Sandbar renewal terms, including termination rights and accrual.
- Lease and Mossvale analysis on whether consent is required for the share sale.
- Independent title and encumbrance searches, not only the internal register.

**Internal actions:**
- Confirm with Amelia Frost in writing before any fallback (cap, 18 months, or post-completion Riverlark release) is offered, identifying the specific draft.
- Reconcile the Seller's clause numbering against the full SPA draft.
- Obtain legal review on NSW law points, particularly the Fundamental/Title regime, fraud carve-out enforceability, and the disclosure drafting.
- Treat tax and IP as separate workstreams, not resolved through the general regime.
